evals.prompt: Should we run the $2M pilot before committing $20M to full development? Build the decision tree with expected values for commit-now, do-nothing and pilot-first, and tell me what the pilot's information is actually worth.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Frames the options including do nothing / wait and the staged pilot-then-decide branch; Lays out chance nodes with probabilities that sum to 1 and payoffs on one basis (NPV), stating the risk attitude; Rolls the tree back to an EV per option and names the optimal policy including the contingent choice after each pilot result; Computes EVPI and the EVSI of the pilot against its cost with an explicit run/skip verdict (EVSI <= EVPI); Reports the risk profile of the recommendation and the switching point, and hands the pilot design to cheapest-experiment.

Lays out chance nodes with probabilities that sum to 1 and payoffs on one basis (NPV), stating the risk attitude
Rolls the tree back to an EV per option and names the optimal policy including the contingent choice after each pilot result
Computes EVPI and the EVSI of the pilot against its cost with an explicit run/skip verdict (EVSI <= EVPI)
Reports the risk profile of the recommendation and the switching point, and hands the pilot design to cheapest-experiment

evals.prompt: Compute the expected value of perfect information for this go/no-go: p(success) 0.4, payoff $60M if it works, $5M if not, $20M to build. Is a market study worth paying for?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Rolls back the go/no-go to its EV and identifies the best option without information; Computes EVPI = EV with perfect information minus best EV and reports it as the ceiling on any study's value; Explains that a study is worth buying only if its EVSI exceeds its cost and shows the arithmetic, ideally with scripts/dtree.py.
expectations: Rolls back the go/no-go to its EV and identifies the best option without information
Computes EVPI = EV with perfect information minus best EV and reports it as the ceiling on any study's value
Explains that a study is worth buying only if its EVSI exceeds its cost and shows the arithmetic, ideally with scripts/dtree.py

evals.prompt: Which uncertainty is my launch decision most sensitive to? I have a decision tree with probabilities and payoffs and want a tornado ranking plus the switching probability where the recommendation flips.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Runs one-way sensitivity on every probability and payoff and ranks inputs by swing (tornado); Reports the switching point at which the optimal branch changes; Says which inputs deserve estimation effort or a test before the commitment.

Says which inputs deserve estimation effort or a test before the commitment
